title: Gymnogeophagus labiatus and G. lacustris ddRADseq Library Protocol
author: Fagundes, Nelson
license_note: Zenodo record metadata license field: cc-by-4.0

steps.title: Extract genomic DNA
steps.instruction: Extract genomic DNA from each specimen using the CTAB method adapted from Doyle & Doyle (1987).

steps.title: Quantify DNA and select samples
steps.instruction: Measure DNA concentration with a Qubit™ 3 fluorometer and retain only samples with concentrations ≥ 30 ng/µl.

substeps.instruction: Load each DNA extract into the Qubit 3 fluorometer according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Record the concentration; discard or set aside any extract below 30 ng/µl.

steps.title: Construct RAD‑Seq libraries
steps.instruction: Build two RAD‑Seq libraries following the double‑digestion protocol of Peterson et al. (2012) using the restriction enzymes SphI and MluCl.

substeps.instruction: Perform double digestion of each qualified DNA sample with SphI and MluCl as described in the referenced protocol.
Proceed with ligation of adapters, size selection, PCR amplification, and any other steps outlined in the Peterson et al. method.

steps.title: Sequence libraries
steps.instruction: Sequence the completed libraries on an Illumina HiSeq 2500 platform, generating single‑end 100 bp reads.

steps.title: Demultiplex and process reads
steps.instruction: Demultiplex raw sequencing reads and process them using the STACKS software suite.

substeps.instruction: Assign reads to individual samples based on barcode sequences.
Run the appropriate STACKS modules (e.g., process_radtags) to clean and filter the data.

steps.title: Run POPULATIONS analysis
steps.instruction: Execute the POPULATIONS module in STACKS with missing‑data thresholds of ≤ 25 % per unlinked locus and ≤ 10 % per individual, and apply the --write-single-snp flag to retain only one SNP per locus.

substeps.instruction: Set the maximum missing data per locus to 25 % and per individual to 10 %.
Include the --write-single-snp option to output a single SNP per locus.
